title: Chronus: Understanding and Securing the Cutting-Edge Industry Solutions to DRAM Read Disturbance
problem: The DDR5 Per Row Activation Counting (PRAC) RowHammer mitigation introduces non-trivial DRAM access latency overhead (counter increment in critical path) and is vulnerable to the 'wave attack' adversarial pattern, forcing overly conservative refresh thresholds that degrade performance.
motivation: DRAM cell shrinkage increases RowHammer vulnerability each generation; despite PRAC being the first in-DRAM standard mitigation, no rigorous security and performance analysis existed, and its overheads become prohibitive for future DRAM generations.
method: Chronus is an on-DRAM-die RowHammer mitigation that separates activation counters from data arrays, allowing counter updates to proceed concurrently with data accesses (eliminating the latency penalty). It also dynamically controls the number of preventive refreshes issued per back-off signal to neutralize the wave attack — which forces repeated activation bursts to exhaust a fixed-refresh budget. The mechanism requires only in-DRAM modifications and is open-sourced.
key_novelty: Decoupling activation counters from data storage arrays enables concurrent counter updates during memory accesses, eliminating PRAC's critical-path latency penalty while dynamic refresh count control defeats wave attacks.
contributions: First rigorous security, performance, energy, and cost analysis of the DDR5 PRAC RowHammer mitigation framework.
Identification of two PRAC weaknesses: critical-path counter latency and vulnerability to the wave attack pattern.
Chronus: concurrent counter update mechanism (counters separated from data arrays) eliminating PRAC latency overhead.
Dynamic preventive refresh count control in Chronus defeating wave attacks; near-zero performance overhead for modern DRAM, very low for future DRAM.

metrics.speedup: Near-zero performance overhead for modern DRAM chips; very low overhead for future chips
metrics.other: Outperforms 3 PRAC variants and 3 other state-of-the-art read disturbance solutions

baselines: Three other state-of-the-art DRAM read disturbance solutions
limitations: Chronus requires modifications to the DRAM die itself, which depends on DRAM vendor cooperation and may face integration challenges with existing DDR5 supply chains.
primary_theme: On-DRAM-die RowHammer mitigation with concurrent counter updates and adaptive refresh
